consensus_summary: Covenant is primarily a solemn, divinely initiated and binding relationship or promissory arrangement between God and his people, involving obligations and culminating in the new covenant.
book_summary: Covenant is primarily the binding and governing word imposed by a head—expressed through law, promises, and judgments—by which a subordinate relationship is established and ruled.
consensus_core_identification: A binding relationship or relational arrangement initiated by God.
book_core_identification: The authoritative word and terms by which a covenant head establishes and governs a relationship.
boundary_disagreement: The book excludes contracts negotiated among autonomous equals from the defining model and treats hierarchy under a covenant head as essential. More fundamentally, it relocates the term from the relationship or agreement itself to the governing word that creates and orders that relationship.
material_contradiction: The consensus identifies covenant with the binding relationship or arrangement; the book identifies it with the head’s binding word, treating the relationship as what that word establishes and governs. These are causally connected but distinct referents.
rationale: This is not merely a more precise description of the same relational category. The book makes the consensus’s covenant—the relationship—the product of covenant understood as authoritative word. Although both readings cover Sinai, covenant blood, obligations, and the new covenant, they assign the term’s core identity to different things.
strongest_objection: The cited texts strongly connect covenant with spoken, commanded, and written words, especially Deuteronomy 4:13, but they may not prove that covenant denotes only the governing word rather than the larger bond or arrangement that includes those words.
